passage:
In the building corner of a kindergarten in Oslo, Ingrid and Oskar were stacking wooden blocks into a tower. “My turn!” Oskar said, grabbing the last flat block. “No, mine!” said Ingrid, pulling. The tower wobbled. Mila watched with wide eyes as it crashed. Both children shouted.

The teacher knelt beside them. “Oh no. What can we do so everyone can put one block?” Ingrid sniffled. “I go, then Oskar.” They built again, slowly, taking turns, and Mila got to put the roof on top.

qa.q: Who grabbed the last flat block?
qa.a: Oskar grabbed the last flat block.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid and Oskar both shout when the tower crashed?
qa.a: Both were frustrated and upset because each had wanted the turn and the pulling made the tower fall.

qa.q: What question did the teacher ask that helped?
qa.a: The teacher asked what they could do so everyone can put one block.

qa.q: How might Mila have felt watching the tower crash with wide eyes?
qa.a: Mila probably felt startled and a bit worried, perhaps wanting a turn, and was happy to place the roof at last.

grounding: Young children build a block tower together and argue over who places what, and an adult helps them take turns.

passage:
At the preschool's block corner, Tejas hugged the red truck. Ishita reached out. “I want it!” “Mine!” Tejas turned his back. Ishita's lip trembled. Rohan, sitting nearby, kept stacking blocks and said nothing.

Their teacher came with a small sand timer. “Tejas has the truck until the sand runs out. Then Ishita. Meanwhile, Ishita, can you load the blocks?” Ishita loaded. When the sand ran out, Tejas held out the truck. “Together?” he said, and they drove blocks across the mat.

qa.q: What did the teacher bring?
qa.a: The teacher brought a small sand timer.

qa.q: Why did Tejas turn his back?
qa.a: Tejas was afraid of losing the truck and wanted to keep it, so turning away was a way to protect it.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped both children?
qa.a: The teacher set a sand timer for Tejas's turn and gave Ishita a job loading blocks meanwhile.

qa.q: What might Ishita have been feeling with the trembling lip?
qa.a: Ishita was probably upset and left out, wanting the truck and fearing there would be no turn.

grounding: Young children argue over a toy truck used to carry blocks, and a teacher's help makes turn-taking and building together possible.

passage:
At the preschool in Cape Town, Xin and Lindiwe were building a tall tower of wooden blocks.
“My turn!” Lindiwe grabbed the red block.
“No, mine!” Xin pulled it back. The tower wobbled.
Both started to cry.
Ms Dlamini knelt beside them. “One block each. Xin, then Lindiwe. I'll count.”
Xin put a blue block on top. Lindiwe put the red one. They looked at each other.
“Again!” said Lindiwe.
The tower grew taller than their heads. When it finally fell, they both screamed with laughter.

qa.q: What colour block did Lindiwe grab?
qa.a: The red block.

qa.q: How did Xin and Lindiwe feel when the tower finally fell?
qa.a: They were delighted and happy, screaming with laughter together.

qa.q: How did Ms Dlamini help them build together?
qa.a: She knelt with them, gave a simple one-each rule and counted turns, so they could share instead of fight.

qa.q: How might Ms Dlamini have felt watching the tower grow?
qa.a: She was probably pleased and relieved to see them taking turns and laughing together.

grounding: Shows young children arguing over a block tower and learning, with adult help, to take turns and build together.

passage:
In the play corner of the community centre, Noor and Irawati were building a castle from big foam blocks.
Irawati put the door on the side. Noor pulled it off. “No, the door goes in front!”
“It's MY castle!” Irawati shouted.
The helper aunty came over. “What if Noor makes the front and Irawati makes the back? Then it's your castle together.”
Noor built the front. Irawati built the back. Once, Irawati handed Noor a block without being asked.
When their mothers came, both girls pointed at the same time. “We made it!”

qa.q: Where did Irawati put the door?
qa.a: She put the door on the side.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel when Noor pulled the door off?
qa.a: She felt angry and upset, shouting that it was her castle.

qa.q: What did the helper aunty's idea do well?
qa.a: It split the job so each girl had her own part of one shared castle, which turned the fight into teamwork.

qa.q: How might the mothers feel when the girls pointed together?
qa.a: They were likely happy and proud to see the two playing together.

grounding: Shows young children arguing over building a castle and, with an adult's help, sharing the job and building together.

passage:
Monday: In the sandpit, Vandana and Vinita both wanted to build the tower. They pushed each other's sand. The tower fell. Both cried.
Wednesday: Their teacher sat with them. “Vandana, one spade. Then Vinita, one spade.” They took turns. The tower got as high as their knees. When Vinita knocked it by mistake, Vandana shouted, but the teacher helped them start again.
The next Monday: No teacher nearby. Vandana said, “My spade.” Then she stopped, and said, “Your spade.” Vinita patted the sand. They took three turns each before arguing about the flag.

qa.q: How high did the tower get on Wednesday?
qa.a: It got as high as their knees.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel when Vinita knocked the tower?
qa.a: She felt angry and upset, and she shouted.

qa.q: What does the next Monday show about learning to take turns?
qa.a: It shows the girls starting to take turns by themselves, though it still breaks down, so adult help is still needed.

qa.q: How might Vinita have felt when Vandana said "Your spade"?
qa.a: She was probably pleased and surprised, patting the sand happily.

grounding: Shows young children, over several days, learning with adult help to take turns building together, though it is still fragile.

passage:
It was raining, so all five children were stuck in the small playroom with one tub of blocks. Akash and Tarun started a tower together.
"Red one here!" Akash said.
"No, mine goes there!" Tarun grabbed it. The tower wobbled. Akash's lip shook. Diya and Ravi watched from the corner.
Mira aunty sat down between the boys. "One block for Akash, one block for Tarun. Let's count."
Slowly they took turns. At twelve blocks the tower stood tall. Tarun clapped. Akash put the last block on top, very carefully.

qa.q: How many blocks tall was the tower when it stood tall?
qa.a: Twelve blocks.

qa.q: What does Akash's shaking lip suggest?
qa.a: Akash felt upset and frustrated when Tarun grabbed the block and the tower wobbled.

qa.q: How did Mira aunty help the boys take turns?
qa.a: She sat between them and made turns simple and fair, one block each, and counted with them.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel when the tower stands tall?
qa.a: Tarun feels proud and happy, clapping for the tower they built together.

grounding: Shows young children arguing over who places which block, with an adult helping them take turns, the seed of teamwork.
